reason: Credit support to AI cloud partners under the revenue-sharing/credit-support programme is a programme inside q09's financing-commitments-and-backstops total, checked in the same FY2027 10-K, and the credit-risk clause is interpretation the amount check does not rest on (boundary 1, R2-e; as adjudicated for dev-d2/d3 clean-1).
The CPU-to-GPU attach ratio in AI inference is a figure no reference question asks about.
Vera Rubin's first shipments by the end of calendar 2026 is the same event and the same deadline as q07's Rubin generation shipping by December 31, 2026.
Huawei/SMIC Ascend unit output in 2026 is a separate figure that no reference question asks about; q17 (NVIDIA's China share) is settled by a different number.

The 'i.e.' clause makes Beijing's permission for Chinese buyers to take H200s the check, with the same deadline (FY2027 year-end, late January 2027), so the same Chinese authorization settles both; actual sales resuming is a later step of that one permission process (R2-f).
The big four hyperscalers' combined calendar-2027 data-center capex is q13's figure; the ~$1 trillion level is a threshold on that same number, and the 2026 level is only a reference point.

First shipment of Kyber NVL144 (Rubin Ultra) racks is q18's event under a later deadline, since a 2028 first shipment is q18's no (boundary 2), and NVL576 volume is a later configuration of the same generation that the check does not rest on (boundary 3; as adjudicated for dev-d3 clean-5).

Supply/purchase commitments (about $119 billion of obligations to buy components and capacity) are a different reported figure from q09's financing commitments and backstops to customers and partners; the two only partly share scope and can move apart.
The outcome of the French competition authority's antitrust probe is an event no reference question covers.
New HBM capacity added in 2027 is a supply figure with its own check, separate from q05's 2027-vs-2026 DRAM/HBM contract-price change, so it could resolve on its own.

It asks how big-four hyperscaler AI accelerator spending in 2027 splits between custom ASICs and NVIDIA GPUs, whereas q16 is cloud providers' custom-silicon spending in 2026 (and q06 is NVIDIA's 2026 share); the year and the measured figure both differ.
Escalation of US export restrictions on AI chips shipped to third countries is a different authority and event from q08's Chinese import authorization, and no reference question covers it.
